messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: Re :Re: ggplot2 graphical interface
parts:
Cedric,

Thanks for contributing this. I myself am in the formulation stages of
adding ggplot2 graphics in a GUI environment. Though I'm working in
java (see the Deducer package).

As a proof of concept your work is very promising. Here are my initial thoughts:

1. I first had to download gtk+, and could not get it working within
the Mac R Gui, or the terminal. I switched to X11, and had some
success, though I get the message:
(R:1191): Gtk-CRITICAL **: gtk_combo_box_append_text: assertion
`GTK_IS_LIST_STORE (combo_box->priv->model)' failed
upon running the example. Though the functionality seems to work okay.

2. I was able to create a scatter plot very easily, and I liked that
the plotting command was shown in the terminal.

3. I was also able to build layers, adding a smoothed line without
trouble. It is very easy to use from the perspective of someone who
knows ggplot2.

4. The initial ggplot2usr dialog is very general, and provides a
direct mapping of the ggplot2 grammar to the GUI elements. Since this
is a package aimed at beginners, I would also create dialogs
specifically geared towards common types of graphs that they are
interested in. Imagine a person who barely knows what a scatter plot
or histogram is. They may be overwhelmed by the options (i.e. what is
an aes?, what does geom <> stat mean?).

5. Think about the tasks that your users are coming to your system
with. What do they sit down wanting to accomplish? Do they want to
compare two continuous variables? make a histogram? look a the density
of a variable overlayed over a map? Then for each task, write a dialog
that does the task with minimal complexity.

6. The drop down list method of selecting variables becomes very
cumbersome when there are lots of variables. most of the datasets I
work with have more than 300 variables.

7. I've found that dialog memory is very important. If I go from geom
point to smooth, then back again, all the options that I set up are
erased.

8. Also, keep in mind what happens when your windows are resized.

This is a good first effort. I look forward to seeing any subsequent versions.

Cheers,
Ian

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Re :Re: ggplot2 graphical interface
parts:
Hi,

My personal taste is not for GUIs but I can see how it may help some
people use ggplot2 without a steep learning curve (coming from, e.g.,
Excel or Origin).

In my opinion the interface could use some icons to help the user
recognise the geoms, aesthetics, etc. A bit like the icons displayed
on Hadley's website. Ideally, these icons could serve as a limited
preview of what the button will do to the graph (i.e. have tunable
parameters).

Best,

baptiste

messages.subject: Re: Re :Re: ggplot2 graphical interface
parts:
I think its a good idea if it introduces people to the grammar and
helps them learn the command line (which it sounds like it does). If
the intention is that people can use this without ever learning the
command line then there's going to be a big user support cost, as
people bump up against the limitations of the GUI...
